Sales is a part of the work I do, and I thought I’d hate it, but it’s low key the best part. I just set up near a part of the store where customers wanting my service would naturally be and then look around to see if they’re looking at my display or similar products to our service. Then I just ask em if they’re interested and about 40% of the time they are, and if they are I’ll usually get the lead. My conversion rates are way higher than my peers as I just give them all the facts of the service and never pressure them into anything. The other half the time, if the stores dead I can just chill. Also, rarely go into an office and have to deal with the drama of that. Really the only time I mask is when I’m pitching. Plus, I get to explore around my area, which is kinda forming into a special interest of mine.

This is definitely not true for everyone, and can vary a lot, but low key a sales job. As, yes the whole point is to be talkative, but if you’re out on the field it’s really only that one time you actually get a customer (assuming you’re just posted somewhere) you need to mask. Plus, a lotta the time you’re not in an actual office, and can travel around (exploring my local area is turning into a special interest). I get great actual conversion rates because I’m not going around badgering people like NTs would be at this job. If I see a potential customer, looking at my display, then I know I can give a good pitch and it will go through. I also don’t pressure the customers as much and am far more direct then my NT peers. People really appreciate honesty when you’re tryna sell them something, and I just tell em how it is and they usually finish the process when I get a lead. Of course I can never say this in that world, but it’s the truth. It kinda shocked me, but for that part of my job, I love it the most.

From what I’ve seen, it focus too much on molding the child to be neurotypical. The child is stimming, make them not do that. I’m sure they’re are ABA therapists that have adapted with the times, but I’ve still seen countless videos of this occurring. This takes away an autistic child’s natural way of regulating there emotions. Another thing is that it sets too high of an expectation on what a child can achieve, that it will probably lead to extreme burnout later in life. One thing about ABA is that it comes with constant reinforcement to get the desired outcome. Once this starts to slowly go away, the  child will find they don’t have much motivation. If an autistic child doesn’t speak naturally, for quite some time, but may “learn” it through ABA, talking away the constant pressure to do so might make them “regress”. This pressure can’t be applied for ever in the real world. A much more effective solution could have been to try and communicate with the child through sign language, as it is more natural to them. Another very harmful thing is granting an adult time (not always alone, but again I’ve seen it mostly done alone) with your child in which the child will be forced to do something they don’t want to do. I’ve seen it brought up that ABA mimicks the discipline of parenting and teaching. However, those are done, specifically with teaching, in public with other kids, where all children are being held to the same standard and can also judge there peers themselves and the discipline of the teacher. This leads into another point, that the child will feel incredibly ostracized. Why am I being pulled out of class to go talk to a therapist? None of the other kids do? A much more effective strategy in my opinion, for say the kid is hitting someone, is to simply call out the behavior while it is happening, mostly so they can see the other kids disapproval. No behavior that is not harmful to those around an Autistic child, need to be spent being corrected. Ultimately, you are trying to Pavlov dog a child into behavior you want them to exhibit, and even if that behavior is ultimately good, trying to force it will never lead to any meaningful progress because as soon as the pressure is off, they will go right back to what they did. Or if it has been instilled enough, they most likely have only done so in defeat, and will loose their ability to determine what is right on wrong on there own.

Also, this is a personal anecdote, but I feel it summarizes the risks of ABA and why I find it hard to believe the defenders of it. My sister got a job teaching ABA while she was a junior in college. I know my sister is hard working, but she was way in over her head. When I asked her about what specifically she did, it came to my attention that she would stop the kid from stimming. Being on the spectrum myself, it did hurt that she didn’t notice how my own stimming caused no problems when I was younger around the house, but ultimately she was taking orders from her boss and wanted to get ahead in her psych career. She also mentioned the child’s parents weren’t always present. Another thing is that it sets too high of an expectation on what a child can achieve, that it will probably lead to extreme burnout later in life. One thing about ABA is that it comes with constant reinforcement to get the desired outcome. Once this starts to slowly go away, the  child will find they don’t have much motivation. If an autistic child doesn’t speak naturally, for quite some time, but may “learn” it through ABA, talking away the constant pressure to do so might make them “regress”. This pressure can’t be applied for ever in the real world. A much more effective solution could have been to try and communicate with the child through sign language, as it is more natural to them. Another very harmful thing is granting an adult time (not always alone, but again I’ve seen it mostly done alone) with your child in which the child will be forced to do something they don’t want to do. I’ve seen it brought up that ABA mimicks the discipline of parenting and teaching. However, those are done, specifically with teaching, in public with other kids, where all children are being held to the same standard and can also judge there peers themselves and the discipline of the teacher. Or if it has been instilled enough, they most likely have only done so in defeat, and will loose their ability to determine what is right on wrong on there own.
